atoms.b: Writing in Egypt originated in around 3000 BC. At its core, it consisted of simple ((cymbals ++symbols)).
For more difficult ((++words dishes)), a combination of several symbols would be used.
We call these symbols ((++hieroglyphs birolifts)), and they formed part of a complex writing system.

feedback.finish: The word hieroglyph comes from ancient Greek and means “sacred carving”.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: The symbols were originally carved into tablets made of stone, wood or wax. Later, hieroglyphs were written on papyrus scrolls with brushes and ink.
Papyrus is a plant that grows well on river banks, such as the Nile. It was turned into a form of paper by cutting it into strips, pressing them together and then letting them dry.
Hieroglyphs could be written in any direction and puzzled archaeologists for a long time. It was not until 1822 that hieroglyphic writing was translated.

atoms.a: What tool was used to write hieroglyphs on papyrus?
How was papyrus turned into paper?
b: by boiling it in hot water

text.text: The human and animal figures in the hieroglyphs show you the direction to read in. In this case, they are all facing to the right, so the text is read from right to left.

atoms.text: Here you can see some Egyptian hieroglyphs and their pronunciations.
